thread:
matt.k: Customer ACME (acme-inc) opened a ticket — indexer rejecting most of their ingest after a model swap. They say embeddings used to be length 1024, new model returns 1536. Indexer returns a vector size error and the backfill triggered a billing spike. attaching summary and sample logs.

sara_support: Got the ticket. Can you paste the exact indexer error and a sample request from the customer? They say the backfill was started from their side and then throttled by us.

jess_eng: In prod we've seen this pattern when a model variant changed dims without the client updating. Two quick checks: what model id did the client call (header + body), and does their SDK pin a version? Also any change to batching config (accelerated-batching flag)?

carlos_indexer: From indexer logs:
```
ERROR 2026-05-12T02:12:09Z indexer: insert failed: vector size mismatch: expected=1024 got=1536
WARN  2026-05-12T02:12:09Z indexer: reject_rate=0.94 rejections_per_min=482
ERROR 2026-05-12T02:13:02Z backfill: enqueue failure: oom while compacting shards
```
We rolled back the consumer stream to stop the flow; after that partial inserts succeeded.

ops-oncall: We observed a throughput spike from a concurrent backfill job — ~500 rps to vecdb for ~10m, which blew past our shard throttles and tripped the protective policy (we bumped throttle to 5rps per user). Did the customer flip a flag to 'accelerated-batching'? That would push multi-file concurrent batches.

jess_eng: Repro we asked for (curl):
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"open-embed-1536","input":["hello","world"]}'
```
Check the array length for each vector in the payload and the response's x-embed-dim header.

sara_support: FYI I put ACME on a temporary mitigation: reverted them to model id open-embed-1024 they used before and paused their backfill job. Customer accepted short-term rollback but asked for an IR + migration plan.

jess_eng: Proposed migration/runbook (short):
- confirm canonical model id used by app and make client pin it (SDK change)
- add server-side detection: if incoming vector length != index expected -> reject with helpful error that includes 'expected' and 'found' dims and a link to migration docs
- short term: run a staged backfill to recompute embeddings to 1536 OR
- alternative: keep old index for 1024 vectors and create a new index for 1536, then update routing (requires query-side fanout or hybrid mapping)
- backfill throttles: limit to 50 rps, canary with 1000 ids to check quality + cost

carlos_indexer: Long term: we can make the index accept variable-length vectors by storing dim metadata per-shard and routing inserts, but that's a heavy migration (reorders shards and storage format). For the immediate support path we'll do the two-index approach + routing shim. I'll prepare a script to mark new docs with metadata "embed_dim":1536 so queries can route.

ops-oncall: Note billing anomaly: the sudden mixed-dim backfill inflated embedding unit usage because our batching code mis-attributed tokens when dims changed (units = vectors * dim/256). Created ticket BILL-4723 to reconcile customer bill and apply a temporary credit while we fix attribution.

sara_support: I've told ACME we'll credit the excess for the affected window and provide a reingest checklist. They want an ETA for the indexer change and the canary backfill steps.

jess_eng: ETA: can do the routing shim + two-index canary in ~48h, full variable-dim index is Q3 project. For now I'll send a small client patch + canary playbook.

deploy-bot: :shipit: indexer-service rollback to v3.4.1 completed at 2026-05-12T03:05:10Z

matt.k: Thanks — main action items: (1) billing reconcile + credit (sara), (2) canary backfill plan and run (jess + carlos), (3) short-term client pin + detection (jess), (4) ops throttle adjustments and monitoring (ops-oncall). I'll follow up with a postmortem thread once we close.

sara_support: on it. ping me if customer pushes back.

carlos_indexer: I'll drop a small repro harness and the shard metadata export in the ticket.

ops-oncall: monitoring checks added to ops dashboard: embed_reject_rate, vecdb_rps_by_customer, backfill_job_concurrency. alert if reject_rate > 0.05 for > 5m.

jess_eng: I'll draft the canary runbook and share in #eng-runtime tomorrow morning. :lock:
